detector.name: Accounting Error
detector.vulnerability_knowledge: Accounting errors occur when a protocol's internal records diverge from actual asset movements or when numerical logic fails to reflect the true behavior of tokens. Common root causes include: (1) assuming `transfer`/`transferFrom` moves exactly the requested amount, which breaks with fee-on-transfer or rebasing tokens; (2) updating state before or after external calls in the wrong order, enabling reentrancy or double-counting; (3) using stale cached values (e.g., `totalSupply`, `balanceOf`) instead of reading live balances after transfers; (4) omitting updates to aggregate counters (e.g., `totalSupply`, `rewardsPerToken.lastUpdated`) during edge cases like zero-supply or first deposit; (5) applying fees or rewards on inflated bases that already include prior fees, causing exponential compounding; (6) trusting external price oracles without conversion steps (e.g., wstETH→stETH→WETH); and (7) depositing imbalanced asset ratios into multi-asset pools (Curve, Balancer) without proportional checks, minting fewer LP tokens than the deposited value. Auditors must trace every asset movement, verify that each state variable mirrors on-chain reality at the exact program point, and confirm that formulas match the documented economic model.
checks: Verify that every ERC20 `transfer`/`transferFrom`/`safeTransfer`/`safeTransferFrom` is followed by a balance delta check (`balanceAfter - balanceBefore`) rather than trusting the input amount, especially for tokens that may be fee-on-transfer or rebasing.

Ensure state variables tracking totals (`totalSupply`, `totalAssets`, `totalShares`, `rewardsPerToken.accumulated`, `rewardsPerToken.lastUpdated`) are updated in the same transaction and in the correct order relative to external calls — typically after incoming transfers and before outgoing transfers.

Check that functions returning early on edge conditions (e.g., `_totalSupply == 0`, `block.timestamp < start`) still update baseline timestamps or accumulators so the first user cannot claim unearned rewards.
Confirm that fee or reward calculations use a base that excludes the fee/reward being minted (e.g., `totalShares()` before protocol fee mint) to prevent recursive compounding.

Validate that price-returning functions perform all necessary conversion hops (e.g., wstETH → stETH via `getStEthByWstEth`, then stETH → WETH via Curve/Uniswap oracle) and return the unit the rest of the protocol expects.

Ensure multi-asset liquidity additions (Curve `add_liquidity`, Balancer `joinPool`) compute amounts proportional to the pool’s current balances or target weights instead of dumping raw contract balances.
Verify that `burn`/`_burn` hooks decrement all supply-tracking variables (`totalSupply`, `totalShares`, queue counters) and that no mapping or counter is left stale.

Check that cross-module calls (e.g., `shareManager.mint`, `feeManager.updateState`, `queue.handleReport`) are sequenced so that each module sees a consistent view of state — no module reads pre-update values while another has already written post-update values.

incorrect_example.explanation: The function trusts the input `amount` instead of measuring the actual token balance increase, so fee-on-transfer tokens cause `shares` and `totalShares` to overstate real deposits.

correct_example.explanation: Measuring the actual balance delta (`received`) ensures accounting stays accurate even with fee-on-transfer or rebasing tokens.
